At для точного часу (at nine o’clock), o: At for exact times (at nine o’clock), on for days (on Monday), in for parts of the day (in the morning). Even Leo’s last-minute plan follows the prepositions.
Чим зайнятий кіт: What the cat is up to
Am / is / are + -ing: дія відбувається п: Am / is / are + -ing: the action is happening right now. A cat sitting on a laptop is also “working” in the Present Continuous.
I’m meeting: домовленість, comes out: ро: I’m meeting: an arrangement, comes out: a timetable. I’ll have downloaded: finished before Saturday, and I’ll be losing: in progress at exactly ten.
Досвід, якого краще не мати: An experience you’d rather not have
Have you ever...? питає про досвід, а ha: Have you ever...? asks about experience, and has just hidden shows a fresh result we can see now. We don’t say when, so it’s the Present Perfect.
Скільки можна чекати оновлення: How long can an update take
Have / has been + -ing: почалося в минул: Have / has been + -ing: it started in the past and is still going on (for two hours, since lunch). The perfect tense for anyone waiting for an update.
Wakes, eats, sleeps з -s, бо he. Щоденні: Wakes, eats, sleeps take -s because of he. Daily habits are always in the Present Simple, even if the whole job is sleeping.
My стоїть перед іменником, а mine, yours: My comes before a noun, while mine, yours, ours replace it completely. That’s how a brother’s pizza quickly becomes “ours”.
Much з незлічуваним (milk), many зі зліч: Much with uncountable nouns (milk), many with countable ones (cookies), any in questions, some and a lot of in statements. Oliver honestly went through the whole scale.
Проєкт майже готовий, правда ж?: The project is almost done, isn’t it?
Після ствердження хвостик заперечний (ha: After a positive sentence the tag is negative (haven’t you?), after a negative one it is positive (is it?). The auxiliary verb comes from the sentence itself.
Who ate...? це питання до підмета, тому: Who ate...? is a subject question, so there is no did. But in Where did you put...? and Why do you have...? the usual order applies: question word + do / did + subject.
Myself: дія повертається на того, хто її: Myself: the action goes back to the person doing it (look at myself), and by yourself means “alone, without help”. Sometimes help would have been a good idea.
Who про людей, that / which про тварин і: Who for people, that / which for animals and things, whose means “whose”, where for places. With a comma (Ruby, whose...) we add information the sentence doesn’t really need.
Переказане питання стає звичайним реченн: A reported question becomes a normal sentence: asked if I was, asked what I wanted, with no did and no question mark. The tense moves back: am → was, want → wanted.
Said і told me переказують чужі слова, а: Said and told me report someone’s words, and the tense moves back: can → could, have to → had to. After told we always say who: told me.
Порада, яка трохи запізнилася: Advice that came a bit too late
Shouldn’t have + V3 це докір про минуле,: Shouldn’t have + V3 is a criticism about the past, should is ordinary advice, and ’d better sounds like a warning: “or things will get worse”.
Always cooks: звичка, тому Present Simpl: Always cooks: a habit, so the Present Simple. Is calling and ’s trying: what is happening right now, so the Present Continuous, and that’s where the whole story is.
So do I означає «я теж» у відповідь на с: So do I means “me too” in reply to a positive statement, Neither do I means “me neither” in reply to a negative one. A short answer repeats the auxiliary: No, I don’t.
There is для однини (one egg), there are: There is for singular (one egg), there are for plural (apples, cats). In questions is / are moves to the front: Is there...? Are there...?
If + had + V3, would have + V3: уявне ми: If + had + V3, would have + V3: an imaginary past that never happened. In the mixed type a past condition gives a result now: would still be in bed.
This і these про те, що поруч, that і th: This and these are for things nearby, that and those for things far away. One / ones replaces a noun so we don’t repeat it: that one, those red ones.
Am з I, is з he / she / it, are з you /: Am with I, is with he / she / it, are with you / we / they. The short forms I’m and you’re sound natural, even when a cat is telling you off.
Too small означає «замалий, і це проблем: Too small means “smaller than needed, and that’s a problem”, big enough means “as big as needed”. So and such just add emphasis: such a silly cat.
Used to + V і would + V про звички минул: Used to + V and would + V describe past habits that are gone now. Be used to means “accustomed to”, and get used to means “becoming accustomed”, and Sam is clearly not ready.
Was з I / he / she / it, were з you / we: Was with I / he / she / it, were with you / we / they. This is how we say where someone was and what things were like in the past: I was ill, you were at the match.
Якби ж то кіт умів друкувати: If only the cat could type
Wish + Past Simple про теперішнє, wish +: Wish + Past Simple is about the present, wish + would is about something annoying, and if only + Past Perfect is regret about the past. The essay can’t be saved now.
Прикметники йдуть у порядку думка → розм: Adjectives go in the order opinion → size → age → colour: lovely big old blue. Just and still go after the auxiliary verb, and place comes before time: in the garden all morning.
